# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for the timely reporting, coordination, and review of all operational incidents occurring at AeroPolicy Airport. It ensures that incidents are managed in a manner that prioritizes safety, compliance, and operational continuity. The policy applies to all incidents that affect the safe and efficient operation of the airport, including but not limited to those involving baggage, restricted items, ramp safety, and equipment. The procedures outlined in this policy are intended to ensure that all incidents are documented, investigated, and resolved in a timely and effective manner, with appropriate corrective actions implemented to prevent recurrence.

The scope of this policy includes all incidents that occur on airside, landside, or within the airport's operational areas. It encompasses both minor and major incidents that may impact the safety of personnel, the security of the airport, or the efficiency of its operations. This policy is designed to support the airport's commitment to maintaining a high standard of operational integrity and to ensure that all incidents are handled in accordance with established procedures and regulatory requirements.

## 2. Incident Categories

Operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport are categorized into four main types: baggage incidents, restricted-item incidents, ramp safety incidents, and equipment incidents. Baggage incidents include any events involving lost, damaged, or misplaced luggage, as well as any issues related to baggage handling procedures. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery of prohibited items, such as weapons, explosives, or other hazardous materials, within the airport's controlled areas. Ramp safety incidents refer to any events that pose a risk to the safety of aircraft, ground personnel, or the public, including but not limited to runway incursions, vehicle collisions, or unauthorized access to restricted zones. Equipment incidents involve malfunctions or failures of airport equipment, such as baggage carts, tow tractors, or communication systems, that could impact operational efficiency or safety.

Each incident category requires specific handling procedures and may involve different levels of coordination and escalation. Baggage incidents are governed by AP-BAG-001, which outlines the procedures for reporting, handling, and resolution. Restricted-item incidents are addressed in accordance with AP-SEC-003, which provides guidelines for security response and investigation. The procedures for ramp safety and equipment incidents are outlined in this policy and are subject to the coordination and review processes described in subsequent sections.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All personnel are required to report any operational incident immediately upon discovery. The initial report should be made to the Reporting Staff Member, who is responsible for documenting the incident in the airport's incident reporting system. The Reporting Staff Member must ensure that the incident is accurately described, including the time, location, and nature of the event. In the event of an emergency, the Reporting Staff Member must also initiate the appropriate emergency response procedures as outlined in the airport's emergency management plan.

The first response to an incident is the responsibility of the Reporting Staff Member, who must take immediate action to mitigate any potential risk or impact. This may include securing the area, ensuring the safety of personnel, and preventing further damage. The Reporting Staff Member must also notify the Incident Coordinator of the incident as soon as possible, providing a detailed summary of the event and any initial findings. This ensures that the Incident Coordinator can begin the coordination process and determine the appropriate level of response and escalation.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the management of all operational incidents at AeroPolicy Airport. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record must include all relevant details of the incident, such as the time, location, and nature of the event, as well as any initial findings and actions taken. The Incident Coordinator is also responsible for coordinating the response efforts of all relevant departments and ensuring that all necessary resources are available to address the incident effectively.

The Incident Coordinator must maintain communication with all involved parties, including the Reporting Staff Member, the Airside Duty Manager, and any external agencies that may be required to assist in the incident response. The Incident Coordinator is also responsible for ensuring that all incidents are escalated to the appropriate level of management, as required by the incident category and severity. This includes coordinating with the Airside Duty Manager for incidents involving ramp safety or equipment failures and ensuring that restricted-item incidents are escalated in accordance with AP-SEC-003.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an operational incident, a post-incident review meeting must be conducted to analyze the cause of the incident and determine the necessary corrective actions. This meeting is chaired by the Incident Coordinator and includes representatives from all relevant departments, including the Airside Duty Manager and the Reporting Staff Member. The meeting must be conducted within a reasonable timeframe following the incident, as determined by the Incident Coordinator, to ensure that all relevant information is still available for review.

During the review meeting, the cause of the incident must be thoroughly examined, and any contributing factors must be identified. The meeting must also assess the effectiveness of the initial response and determine whether any procedural or operational deficiencies contributed to the incident. Based on this analysis, corrective actions must be identified and implemented to prevent recurrence. These actions may include changes to procedures, additional training for personnel, or modifications to equipment or systems.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in the airport's incident reporting system and retained for the required period as stipulated by regulatory requirements. Each incident record must include a detailed description of the incident, the actions taken, the personnel involved, and the outcome of the post-incident review. Records must be accessible to authorized personnel and must be reviewed periodically to ensure their accuracy and completeness. The Incident Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all records are properly maintained and that any deficiencies in record-keeping are promptly addressed.
